text: Confirmed: Interval.fromISO parses the duration half with DateTime.fromISO, which throws when Settings.throwOnInvalid is true, so the duration branch is never reached. Fixing it in src/interval.js.
Confirmed: objToLocalTS in src/impl/util.js shifts the year after Date.UTC overflowed the day into a leap year (2000), so 0100-03-02 becomes 0100-03-01. Fixing the year/month/day re-application.
Confirmed: isInDST compares against this.set({month:1}), which in 1974 keeps the January 6 date (already DST), so the comparison fails. Fixing the January reference point.
Duration.normalize producing NaN: root cause is in the unit conversion matrix used by normalizeValues. Fixing it in src/duration.js.
Negative-year ISO formatting: padStart counts the '-' sign as a digit, so -1 renders as "00-1". Fixing the year padding so the sign is emitted separately.
FixedOffsetZone with a non-numeric offset: the constructor never validates the offset, so isValid stays true. Fixing validation in src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js.

Fixed. Interval.fromISO now probes each half with DateTime.fromISO inside a try/catch, so when throwOnInvalid is true the throw no longer prevents the Duration.fromISO fallback. Both "2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00/PT5H30M" and "PT5H30M/2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00" now return the same valid intervals as with throwOnInvalid left at its default. Verified; full suite unchanged (only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures).

Fixed. objToLocalTS (src/impl/util.js) re-applied only the year after Date.UTC had already overflowed the day into year 2000 (a leap year), so 0100-03-02 became 0100-03-01. It now re-applies year, month and day together (setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month-1, obj.day)), resolving the overflow in the target year's calendar. DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({day:61}).toISODate() is now "0100-03-02". Verified against a differential civil-date reference for 2400+ cases; full suite unchanged.

Fixed. isInDST compared against this.set({month:1}), which for a January date is a no-op, so 1974-01-06 compared equal to itself. It now uses Jan 1 / May 1 as the standard-time reference points and also considers the offset at the end of the local day (1974's DST began at 02:00 on Jan 6, so midnight itself is still PST). DateTime.fromISO("1974-01-06", {zone:"America/Los_Angeles"}).isInDST is now true, 1974-01-05 is false, and southern-hemisphere/fixed-offset/invalid cases are unchanged. Full suite unchanged.

Fixed. The conversion matrices in src/duration.js were missing entries (years.quarters and quarters.seconds), so convert() divided by undefined and produced NaN. Added the missing entries in both the casual and longterm matrices; an audit confirms no other unit pair is missing. Duration.fromObject({years:1,quarters:2}).normalize().toObject() and Duration.fromObject({quarters:1,seconds:2}).normalize().toObject() now return numbers (no NaN). All duration tests pass; full suite unchanged.

Fixed. padStart (src/impl/util.js) counted the leading "-" as one of the padded digits, so padStart(-1, 4) gave "00-1". It now emits the sign separately and zero-pads only the absolute value. toISODate() for year -1 is now "-0001-01-01" and for year -10 "-0010-01-01"; positive years and all offset formatting are unchanged. Full suite unchanged.

Fixed. FixedOffsetZone#isValid was hardcoded to true and the constructor never validated the offset. It now returns isNumber(this.fixed), so new FixedOffsetZone("CDT").isValid is false and DateTime.fromMillis(0, {zone}) is invalid with invalidReason "unsupported zone". Valid numeric offsets, UTC, and parseSpecifier are unchanged. Full suite unchanged.
